name: qfd_sys_face-mu1-COMMIT
purpose: MU (4-user) re-close of the compute-die system face: MU D2D image (2nd kind-12 context slot) + filler head contexts. Benches: tb_qfd_sys_face #(MU 1) with the MU image (production 36-layer START table, 1,512 events exact + 4 head contexts users 0..3) and its mutants; MU-KV-CTX end-to-end CAL bench (KV record port MU 1 -> real KV/compute D2D sequencers + calendars with the MU image -> face kind-12 RX + qfd_mu_ctx_rx -> ctlm loader).

structural_change: MU re-close (MU-DQ-SYSFACE 10-19, coordinator 0kg; reroute_reason rtl_change, COORD pre-accepted): Qwen ROM 4-user release. (1) D2D sequencer source-select ot_qwen_d2d_cal_seq_dies.sv -> ot_qwen_d2d_cal_seq_dies_mu.sv = the MU image d2d_cal_image_mu.svh (regenerated on the current die stages: D2D_MU=1 d2d_cal_image_production.sh; C RX + K TX +1 entry = the token-run MU context slot S->C kind 12 beat 1, C RX arrival 18; SEG2 8 -> 9; START / FIRST_TOKEN / PERIOD / TXDP unchanged); constants only. (2) #(MU 1): filler (user 1..3 on tt_native_pos[17:16], MU-DQ-D2DUSER) head contexts are no longer checked against the user-0 HOST tag (the closed face faulted on every filler context); they are checked for a valid installed host epoch + fused cap, position < 8192, token < 151936 (mu_hc_fault, sticky, joins face_fault). User 0 / MU 0 logic unchanged. Same outline, macro, pins and faces as rs3. rs3 text follows: SUCCESSOR rs3 (Q-SYSFACE3 10-18, coordinator 0ea CHANGES REQUESTED on rs2: ROM x 190.08 off the 43.2-um lattice, all-sink spread 94.5 TT / 96.2 FF > 80, util 12%): same RTL as rs2 (emb_prov_fault port + G8 re-port kept), same face assignment (S-face emb_* pins kept); outline 302.4x216 -> 259.2x129.6 (pin-limited by the N face: 1,322 bits now at uniform ~5.5 b/um end to end, every face spread by bit count), ROM on the 43.2 lattice at (172.8, 43.2) R0, a shorter clock tree over half the area for the pin-flop spread. rs2 text follows: SUCCESSOR rs2 (Q-STUB 10-17) = rs1 + the Q-CTLM G8 DV re-port (crom_fault_code / res_issue_fault inputs dropped: their producers left the die) + emb_prov_fault input (qfd_embedding_word_provider.fault was an open output on dv2f11; registered, sticky, joins face_fault in the rst_emb region). pin_reg_split off (current ref_tile gen rejects it without the recipe-2 pin hook; rs1's kit.env never carried it). Re-close needed because the bound view @4458091af carries the 2 dropped pins. rs1 text follows: SUCCESSOR rs1 of qfd_sys_face rr1 (7473dff29, EARLY_FAIL_HOLD at 4_1_cts: FF hold -40.35 -> -28.5 after 10.5k hold buffers, every worst endpoint an N-face input pin flop rx_payload__ot_q[*] behind the recipe-3 input hold pad; CTS 8 bufs / 10 levels, pin-flop arrival 313-404 ps) and of rq1 (CLOSED, native pin audit FAIL rst_n capture 461.9 > 190). STRUCTURAL: (1) recipe 4 / hold_budget die (owner-approved FLOW-HOLD 10-16): flop-first pins, NO input/output hold pads, boundary hold is the die budget at the relay stations; every data pin lands in / launches from a pin register (recipe-3 pin_regs). (2) RTL regional reset rs1: 14 relay flops, each <= 256 loads (rr1 lint: rst_rec 1,153 / rst_out 303 / rst_boot 278); record port reset per sub-block (rtl/qwen_split/qfd_sys_face_record_port.sv, logic identical to qfd_program_record_port), boot control vs PW/DW payload, outputs split events / emb RX / STATUS; same release edge, bench bit-exact (MUT0 1,512 events, MUT1-4 FAIL). (3) Pins re-faced to the die neighbours of Qwen dv2r8f7 (sys_face x 1101.6-1404.0, y 22496.0-22712.0): N = D2D (d2d_rom NW, rs_bump/fwd_epoch bumps N), W = native59 (directly W, full height) + tt_ctlm (SW): host context / native slots / TT faces, S = embed_prov (directly S) + io_collective (far S): embedding provider + io faults, E (was empty) = SU / sequencer observer faces seq_* (no dv2r8f7 bus; E is the compute columns and DV lane relays). Each face spread end to end by bit count. (4) ck at the N-face centre between the two 548-bit record buses (prog_tx_record W of it, rx_payload E of it) = the register mass (~1,300 N pin flops + the record port they feed).
